rules.sentence: In tricuspid regurgitation, lesions fall into 2 categories: primary, where intrinsic abnormalities in the tricuspid valvular apparatus are responsible, and secondary, where right atrial or ventricular dilatation causes tricuspid regurgitation.
The most common cause of tricuspid regurgitation is secondary or functional regurgitation.

Secondary disorders like tricuspid annular dilation and leaflet tethering in right ventricular pressure and volume overload are largely responsible for tricuspid regurgitation compared to primary disorders involving the valve apparatus.[6][7][8]

Dilatation of the right atrium and the right ventricle, along with dilatation of the tricuspid annulus and tethering of the tricuspid valve leaflet, are some of the causes of secondary tricuspid regurgitation.[9]
This may result from conditions affecting the right ventricle or may be due to an increase in right ventricle systolic pressure, often with pulmonary hypertension.

Conditions affecting the right ventricle that eventually cause tricuspid regurgitation include cardiomyopathies and ischemic heart diseases involving the right ventricular myocardium and tricuspid papillary muscles.[10]
